NOW.thesis_one_line: Best-in-class enterprise workflow/AI software franchise growing 21-24%, but after counting about $2.6bn a year of stock compensation as a cost the price implies about 17% annual free-cash-flow growth for ten years (top of a 14-17% base case), net cash has become net debt and a DOJ hiring investigation is still open; revisit below about $110 or on evidence that FCF after SBC tracks the $3.1bn guide.
kill_criteria: Subscription revenue growth decelerates below 18% YoY for two consecutive quarters.

DOJ investigation into the 2023 Army-CIO hiring results in a formal finding against the company (not just the departed executive) or any debarment/suspension action against ServiceNow's federal business.
Trailing-four-quarter non-GAAP free cash flow margin falls below 30% (guide is 35% for FY26; H1 2026 was 29.5%, and single quarters are seasonal so the test is on the trailing year).
Net debt/EBITDA (GAAP) exceeds 2.0x following further debt-funded buybacks or M&A.
Stock-based compensation exceeds 17% of revenue for two consecutive quarters (Q2 2026: 16.4%).
key_adverse_facts: DOJ / DoD-IG / Army Suspension & Debarment Office matter over the March 2023 hiring of the outgoing U.S. Army CIO remains open; the 10-Q (0001373715-26-000076, Note 17) says the Company is cooperating with a DOJ investigation that required document delivery and cannot predict timing, outcome or impact; nothing accrued.

Stock-based compensation was $652m in Q2 2026 (16.4% of revenue) and about $2.19bn over the trailing year, so free cash flow after SBC is about $2.4bn trailing and about $3.1bn on the FY26 guide, a 2.2% yield on the $141bn market cap.

Net debt, not net cash: cash and investments $6.71bn against debt $7.52bn (short-term $2.08bn incl. commercial paper, long-term $5.44bn after $4.0bn of May 2026 notes), while $2.2bn of stock was repurchased in H1 2026 and $8.8bn was spent on acquisitions (Armis, Veza, others).
FY26 free cash flow guide of 35% margin implies about $5.7bn (revenue about $16.2bn); H1 non-GAAP FCF margin was 29.5% against 32% a year earlier, so the second half must run near 43%.
Non-GAAP operating margin guidance was cut from 32% to 31.5% at the Q1 print for Armis dilution while revenue guidance was raised.
data_conflicts: None found vs the b1/d4 quant files themselves, but the pre-registered quant model ranks NOW poorly (decile 1, live_rank 474) purely on value/momentum factors, while the fundamentals (steady 21-24.5% subscription growth, raised guidance three quarters running) do not support a deteriorating business -- the low rank reflects the model's factor tilts, not a fundamental red flag; NOW reached this wave via the triage/quality-growth path, not the live-rank gate.
NOW.confidence_in_thesis: medium-low: business fundamentals and guidance are well verified from primary filings, but the valuation test fails once SBC is a cost and the DOJ matter remains unresolved

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row for NOW. RA9 re-test 6 Oct 2026: the original reverse DCF used a $5.15bn trailing FCF that does not match the filings (operating cash flow $5,308m less capex $728m = $4,580m), added back stock compensation, used a 4.14% ERP and overstated FY26 revenue ($18.5bn versus about $16.2bn). On FY26 guided FCF of about $5.7bn less SBC of about $2.6bn = $3.1bn ($2.98 per share, 1.04bn diluted shares), price $135.62, discount rate 9.8% (5.17% Treasury + 0.98 Blume-adjusted beta x 4.75% ERP; range 9.2-10.5%), terminal growth 3.5%, the price implies 17.0% annual 10-year FCF/share growth after SBC (15.5% at 9.2%, 18.7% at 10.5%) versus a re-based after-SBC base case of 14-17%. Fair value at 16% growth is $126 (-7%). Implied is at or above the top of the base range, so the old 'below/cheap' view is withdrawn.

NOW.scenario_basis: RA9 restated 6 Oct 2026: scenario fair value from 10-year FCF/share-after-SBC growth and discount rate (bear 11% at 10.5%, base 16% at 9.8%, bull 21% at 9.2%; $2.98 base, terminal 3.5%) = $77 / $126 / $206, price converging to scenario value in three years, no dividends. Previous figures were -5.3% / +16.3% / +29%.

NXPI.thesis_one_line: Auto and industrial chip leader in a confirmed three-quarter recovery, fairly priced for that recovery rather than a screaming bargain.
kill_criteria: Quarterly revenue guidance is cut (vs the prior quarter's guide) for the first time since the Q1 FY26 recovery began.
Automotive segment revenue growth (YoY) turns negative for two consecutive quarters.
Non-GAAP gross margin falls back below 56% (below the low end of the Q3 FY26 guide range).
Net debt/EBITDA (approx.) exceeds 2.5x without an offsetting FCF acceleration.
China EV price-war commentary reappears in a quarterly earnings call as a stated headwind to bookings (it was cited as a risk, not yet a reported impact, in the most recent guide).
key_adverse_facts: FY2025 total revenue was down 3% YoY -- a real, recent cyclical trough, not a hypothetical risk.

A large share of the Q1 FY26 GAAP EPS beat ($4.43 vs $1.92 a year earlier) is a one-time $627M gain on the sale of the MEMS Sensors business to STMicroelectronics, not operating leverage; this also inflates the quant model's earnings-momentum (SUE) score for this name.

Gross debt is $11.04B (net debt approx. $7.8B) laddered out to 2035+, real leverage for a cyclical semiconductor business heading into an unresolved cyclical risk (China EV price war, flagged by triage, not yet resolved).
Several small, routine 10b5-1 insider sales by the CFO, COO and Chief People Officer through 2026 -- not judged a material red flag given scale, but disclosed.
data_conflicts: None found. Note for the record: 'Nexperia' (the China/Netherlands chip-export-control and asset-freeze dispute in the news through 2025-2026) is a different, formerly-affiliated company (divested by NXP in 2017, now owned by China's Wingtech) and is not NXP Semiconductors (NXPI) -- flagged to prevent a common secondary-source conflation, not because any NXPI-specific issue was found.
NXPI.confidence_in_thesis: medium: three quarters of primary-source-verified beat-and-raise guidance is a strong pattern, but the base rate for auto/industrial semi cycles reversing quickly is real and the company's own FY2025 revenue decline is recent

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: NXPI has no V1 valuation row this cycle. My own reverse DCF (TTM FCF $3.56B, EV $66.15B, WACC ~11.8%, 10y fade to 3% terminal) implies ~9.6%/yr FCF growth for 10 years, essentially equal to my evidence-based base case of ~9%/yr (mid-to-high-single-digit auto/industrial content growth plus buyback/dividend contribution) -- growth priced in is in line with my base case, a fair rather than clearly cheap valuation despite the low absolute P/E.

SNDK.thesis_one_line: NAND flash maker riding a real AI-datacenter shortage, but the stock already needs that shortage's record margins to keep compounding for a decade.
SNDK.horizon: 12-36 months (re-underwrite when FY2027 guidance clarifies cycle duration)
kill_criteria: Sequential revenue growth turns negative for two consecutive fiscal quarters (vs the +21%/+31%/+97%/+51% sequential path of the last four quarters).
Non-GAAP gross margin falls below 60% (from the current 78.4%, FQ3'26), signalling NAND pricing normalization.
Management commentary shifts from 'bits on allocation beyond 2027' to any statement of easing allocation or customer inventory correction.
Net cash position (currently ~$4.76B, zero debt) reverses into net debt without an offsetting M&A rationale.
Quarterly guidance is met or missed (rather than blown through), signalling the extreme-beat pattern of the last four quarters has ended -- itself a leading indicator the cycle is normalizing.
key_adverse_facts: Extreme earnings volatility: a $1.9B GAAP net loss (quarter ended 28 Mar 2025) swung to $6.9B GAAP net income (quarter ended 3 Jul 2026) within four quarters -- every 'quality' metric the quant model rewards (ROE 91.6%, gross margin 56.5%+) is a cycle-peak snapshot, per the triage note's own red flag, confirmed in primary filings.
~80% of manufacturing capacity runs through the Flash Ventures joint venture with Kioxia -- a single-partner structural dependency, disclosed in the 10-K.
Under two years of independent trading history (spun off from Western Digital 24 Feb 2025); pre-2025 financials are a divisional carve-out, not standalone history.

Every one of the last four quarterly guidance ranges was beaten by a widening margin (revenue beats of +5%, +14%, +24%, +8.7% vs the high end; non-GAAP EPS beats of +36%, +82%, +67%) -- management itself cannot forecast this cycle, which is informative about downside unpredictability as much as upside momentum.
data_conflicts: V1 (`v1_valuation_table.csv`) rates SNDK 'excessive' (implied 10-year growth 29.4% vs consensus FY1 growth 18.3%); this dossier independently corroborates that verdict via a separately-derived, lower-methodology reverse DCF (16-21%/yr implied, using reported OCF-less-capex rather than V1's FCFF-from-EBIT-without-SBC-addback) -- the methodologies disagree on the exact number but agree on the direction and the conclusion.
SNDK.confidence_in_thesis: medium: the near-term fundamentals and guidance-beat pattern are unambiguous and well-sourced, but the multi-year duration of the NAND upcycle -- the entire basis for a favorable long-run verdict -- is inherently uncertain and cannot be verified from filings alone

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: V1's reverse DCF implies 29.4%/yr required FCF growth for 10 years vs consensus FY1 growth of 18.3% (verdict: excessive; 3-year bear/base/bull scenario returns could not be computed by V1, 'insufficient history'). My own simplified reverse DCF using reported OCF-less-capex (rather than V1's FCFF-from-EBIT method, which does not add back SBC) implies a lower but still-demanding 16-21%/yr. Both anchor to a TTM FCF base that is itself a cycle peak, which understates the true bar even further: the price requires peak margins to persist and then compound at a double-digit rate for a decade, a materially higher bar than management's own 'multi-year, not decade-long' shortage framing. I agree with V1: implied growth priced in is above any evidence-based base case.
